trial_title: Onabotulinum Toxin A (Botox) for the Treatment of Persistent Post-Stroke and Vascular Headache
brief_summary: Post stroke headache occurs in approximately 10-23% of all stroke patients. Its onset is shortly after experiencing a stroke, or stroke like event, and persists for at least three months. These headaches have features which resemble migraine or occur in people who have a previous history of migraine that was once infrequent. Botox is a treatment that is currently approved for the treatment of chronic migraine, that is migraine headaches occurring for at least 15 days a month for at least 3 month

eligibility_table.criterion: Adult patients (>18 y) fulfilling ICHD-3 criteria of persistent post stroke/hemorrhagic stroke headache; persistent headache post dissection and post RCVS persistent headache will be enrolled at 3 months or greater of persistence of symptoms.

For the purposes of this study, as suggested elsewhere in the literature, the initial onset of headache will be considered for study if occurring within 72 hours prior to and 7 days post sentinel vascular event ('Stroke'). The 72 hours prior criteria allowing for inclusion of patients of intracerebral hemorrhage who are known to have anticipatory headache as well as alternate ischemic syndromes in which new onset headache may anticipate stroke symptoms such as dissection and reversible cerebro-vasoconstriction syndrome.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of spontaneous intraventricular hemorrhage and a head injury, but there is no specific information about the onset of headache relative to the sentinel vascular event.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Did the patient experience the onset of headache within 72 hours prior to or 7 days post the sentinel vascular event of spontaneous intraventricular hemorrhage?

eligibility_table.criterion: The syndrome of post CVST headache patients will only be enrolled after symptoms have persisted for a minimum of 6 months and after relevant imaging demonstrates a resolution of potentially structural contribution from the sentinel event (i.e. recanalization or chronic thrombo-sis with a normal opening pressure on lumbar puncture).
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has not had symptoms for 6 months post-event, as the timeline of symptoms is unclear.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced persistent headache symptoms for at least 6 months following the resolution of structural contributions as confirmed by relevant imaging?

eligibility_table.criterion: Note the patients of post dissection persistent headaches may be enrolled despite the absence of an identified ischemic lesion, i.e. in the setting of TIA or new onset headache without embolic symptoms but with a history of the (stabilized) vascular injury associated with the syndrome.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's condition does not clearly indicate a history of dissection or persistent headaches related to it.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented history of vascular injury associated with the syndrome despite the absence of an identified ischemic lesion?

eligibility_table.criterion: Note the co-existence of medication overuse headache will not be a contraindication to randomization.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is on pain medication, but there is no indication of medication overuse headache.

eligibility_table.criterion: Tension type Post Stroke Persisting Headache, Post stroke pain syndrome such as the Thalamic syndrome of Dejerine-Roussy, or any headache semiology that does not fulfill diagnostic criteria for chronic migraine, will be excluded.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's headache type is not specified, and it is unclear if it meets the criteria for chronic migraine.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a headache semiology that fulfills the diagnostic criteria for chronic migraine?

eligibility_table.criterion: Contraindications to Botox, neuromuscular illness or documented hyper-sensitivity will preclude randomization of patients.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about contraindications to Botox or any neuromuscular illness.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have any documented history of neuromuscular illness or hypersensitivity to botulinum toxin?

eligibility_table.criterion: Concurrent active systemic illness, such as sepsis, chronic infective processes, neoplastic syndromes, or autoimmune syndromes. (Headache secondary to medical illness, even if occurring post-stroke).
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a significant medical history, but it is unclear if it constitutes an active systemic illness.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have any active systemic illness, such as sepsis, chronic infective processes, neoplastic syndromes, or autoimmune syndromes, as indicated by current lab values or clinical assessment?

eligibility_table.criterion: Subjects must be screened for coexistent (including psychiatric) conditions to exclude illnesses that may influence the conduct or results of the trial. Subjects with coexisting conditions, such as depression, may be included if they are defined a priori, stable on current treatment regimens (with no anticipated changes in management that may interfere with study results), and recorded throughout the study. One of the secondary outcome measures in the study investigates the potential impact on concurrent symptoms of depression. However, the stability of symptoms treatment and concomitant medications should be assessed prior to inclusion in the study. If factors are identified which might interfere with patient compliance, follow up or confound results, such patients should be excluded. Other common reasons for exclusion include severe depression and overuse of alcohol or illicit drugs, as defined by the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th edition.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's psychiatric history is not detailed enough to assess stability or potential confounding factors.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's depression currently stable on a defined treatment regimen with no anticipated changes in management for at least the past 3 months?

eligibility_table.criterion: CGRP inhibitors will be contraindicated during the period of study.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about the use of CGRP inhibitors during the study period.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient been prescribed any CGRP inhibitors in the past 30 days?
